intro: Horizon City has its own police department and its own municipal court, and a ticket there is handled differently than one downtown. For a flat $69, attorney Robert Navar appears in Horizon City Municipal Court for you and works to keep the ticket off your record.

sections.heading: Horizon City Police Tickets and Where They Are Filed
paragraphs: Horizon City is one of the fastest-growing cities in El Paso County, and its police department has grown with it. Officers patrol Darrington Rd, Eastlake Blvd, Horizon Blvd, Kenazo Ave and the subdivisions filling in around them, and they write a steady volume of speeding, stop-sign, school zone, no insurance and registration citations. Every one of those is filed in Horizon City Municipal Court, which is a City of Horizon City court with its own judge, clerk and prosecutor.

The city limits matter. The Horizon area is a patchwork: the same stretch of road can pass from Horizon City jurisdiction into unincorporated county or into the City of El Paso within a mile. A Sheriff's deputy or DPS trooper who stops you on the same road files in a Justice of the Peace precinct, and an El Paso police officer files in El Paso Municipal Court. The agency name on your citation tells you which court has the case; if you are not sure, use our free ticket and warrant lookup.

sections.heading: How Horizon City Municipal Court Runs Its Docket
paragraphs: Horizon City Municipal Court is a smaller court than its El Paso counterpart. It holds traffic dockets on a limited schedule rather than every day, and the same prosecutor and judge see the same cases from start to finish. Verify the current docket schedule with the court if you plan to go yourself; the dates change, and arriving on the wrong day can mean waiting weeks for the next setting.

That schedule is the main reason a lawyer helps here. When you hire us, we file a notice of appearance and a not-guilty plea before your appearance date. The court then places the case on its next pretrial docket, and Robert Navar or a member of our staff attends, confers with the city prosecutor and negotiates. You do not need to take a morning off work or drive out to Darrington Rd. Any continuance and the next docket are covered by the same flat fee.

Smaller courts also mean the officer who wrote the ticket is well known to the court, and the case tends to be evaluated on its facts. When a citation has a defect — a wrong statute, a missing speed, an unclear location — the prosecutor is usually willing to hear it out and dismiss rather than set a trial the department does not want.

sections.heading: What the Horizon City Prosecutor Typically Offers
paragraphs: Horizon City Municipal Court follows the same Texas rules as every other Class C court. Deferred disposition under Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45.051 is available for most moving violations: pay a special expense fee, stay violation-free for 90 to 180 days, and the case is dismissed with no conviction and no report to DPS. The driving safety course dismissal under art. 45.0511 is available to eligible drivers who were not cited 25 mph or more over the limit, do not hold a CDL, and have not used the course in the past 12 months. Details and eligibility are on our deferred adjudication and defensive driving page.

Because Horizon City has many school zones along Darrington Rd, Eastlake Blvd and Kenazo Ave, school-zone speeding is one of the most common tickets we see from the city, and the court is careful about offering course dismissals for those. We ask for deferred disposition instead, or for a reduction to a non-moving charge when the client's record makes deferral unlikely. Compliance tickets — insurance, registration, license — are typically dismissed when we show the problem has been fixed.

sections.heading: Our $69 Flat Fee for Horizon City Municipal Court
paragraphs: We charge $69 per citation in Horizon City Municipal Court. The fee covers the appearance, every docket setting and the paperwork to close the case; any court fee for a deferral or course is paid to the court separately. Additional citations from the same stop are discounted $10–$30 add-ons on the online hire page. If you already have a Horizon City warrant, it is $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional, and we handle the recall together with the ticket.

Paying the ticket instead means a conviction, two points on your Texas record, and higher insurance at every renewal for three years. For a family with two or three cars insured together, one conviction can affect the whole policy. sections.heading: Horizon City Warrants and Missed Court Dates
paragraphs: If your Horizon City appearance date passes without a filing, the court issues a warrant and adds a separate failure to appear charge under Transportation Code 543.009. Horizon City also reports unresolved cases to the state's Failure to Appear program, so an OMNI hold can block your license renewal at DPS until the court clears it. Because the court meets on a limited schedule, a self-represented driver who shows up to fix it can wait longer than in El Paso.

We file the appearance, request the warrant recall and ask the court to reset the ticket on the next docket — the same process we describe on the traffic warrant recall page. Once the ticket is back on a docket it is handled like any other case.

sections.heading: What to Do After a Horizon City Ticket
paragraphs: Note the appearance date on the citation, do not pay it and do not request defensive driving on your own — that request is a plea. Send us the citation through the online form or call 915-503-1600, and have your license and current insurance card ready. We will confirm the court, the fee and the plan the same day.
This page is general information, not legal advice about your case. Verify current docket dates with Horizon City Municipal Court, or let our office do it for you.

faqs.q: Which tickets go to Horizon City Municipal Court?
faqs.a: Citations written by the Horizon City Police Department inside the city limits. Tickets from Sheriff's deputies, DPS troopers or constables in the same area go to an El Paso County Justice of the Peace precinct instead.

faqs.q: What is the attorney fee for a Horizon City ticket?
faqs.a: A flat $69 per citation. Extra tickets from the same stop are discounted add-ons, and warrant recalls are $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional one.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to court in Horizon City?
faqs.a: In most cases, no. We file the appearance and attend the docket for you. You would only need to appear if the case were set for trial, which is uncommon and something we would discuss first.

faqs.q: Does Horizon City Municipal Court allow deferred disposition?
faqs.a: Yes, for most ordinary moving violations. School-zone, 25+ mph over and CDL cases are treated more strictly, which is where having a lawyer make the request rather than asking yourself tends to matter.

faqs.q: I missed my Horizon City court date. Is there a warrant?
faqs.a: Probably, and possibly an OMNI hold on your license renewal. Call us the same day; we file the appearance, request the recall and get the ticket back on a docket — see traffic warrant recall.

faqs.q: I live in Horizon City but an El Paso officer wrote the ticket. Which court?
faqs.a: El Paso Municipal Court downtown, because the issuing agency decides the court, not your address. Our fee there is $59. Use the free lookup form if you are unsure.
